newsitem.title: USA: Tyco to buy AT&T submarine systems business.
newsitem.headline: Tyco to buy AT&T submarine systems business.

text.p: Tyco International Ltd., a diversified commercial and industrial manufacturer, said Friday it agreed to buy AT&T Corp.'s undersea telecommunications cable unit for about $850 million.
The unit to be acquired, AT&T Submarine Systems Inc., makes undersea fiber optic telecommunication cable systems.
Tyco, based in Exeter, N.H., operates in more than 50 countries. It manufactures disposable medical products, packaging materials, flow-control products, and electrical and electronic components.
It also makes and installs fire and safety systems, and last month bought home security company ADT for $5.4 billion.
Tyco projected the submarine cable unit's 1997 revenues at about $1 billion.

"The acquisition will have an immediate positive impact on our earnings, as well as providing substantial long-term benefits to Tyco," said L. Dennis Kozlowski, Tyco's chairman and chief executive officer.

Tyco's Simplex Technologies unit, a major manufacturer of undersea fiberoptic telecommunications cable, has produced enough undersea fiberoptic cable to circle the globe four times, the company said. Most of the cable has been purchased and installed by AT&T's Submarine Systems unit and the U.S. Navy.
In a statement announcing the sale, AT&T President and Chief Operating Officer John Walter said it ensures that AT&T's portfolio includes only businesses key to its communications services strategy.
AT&T's stock slipped 37.5 cents to $34.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Tyco lost 25 cents to $58, also on the NYSE.
